label: sparse end-of-input / start-of-copy feature in long sequences beginning with q or l
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.03% of steps). Activation mass sits at the boundary between input and copy: the last one or two original tokens of long sequences (L=8-9; t=8 with L=9 alone holds ~43% of mass), the <DEL> step, and the first copy step (input = the fed-back first token). It is strongly enriched when the first original token is q (59% of mass, 18x lift) or l (18%, 5x). The strongest activations come at the final original token of L=9 sequences and short sequences starting with q at recall_idx 1. It never fires at t<=3, and almost never fires after recall_idx 3 or on incorrect copies. Even so, it is far from deterministic: within the best context (first_tok q, L=9, t=8) it fires only ~10% of the time, and which sequences fire seems to depend on the particular mix of tokens in the sequence (p, z, g, j, r, 2 are enriched), which I could not capture. The predicate covers ~75% of activation mass with precision of ~1.4%.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=q (+4.74), orig0=q (+4.53), orig0=l (+3.40), orig2=p (+2.92), orig1=m (+2.80), t=8 (+2.56). Lower it: phase=2 (-2.84), t=3 (-2.83), prev3_tok=- (-2.82), to_go=5 (-2.47).
